data.narrative:
Lux Aeterna is a Seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Brian Taylor, a veteran of SpaceX Starlink, Amazon Project Kuiper, and Loft Orbital. The company has raised $14M to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public Space & Aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private comparables including SpaceX, Sierra Space, Planet Labs, Impulse Space, and Apex Space.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the $14M in total capital raised as a proxy for baseline valuation and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement in the sector, yielding $35M. Peer-Median triangulation was not feasible due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables in Space & Aerospace (zero same-stage and zero adjacent-stage peers meeting filter criteria, below the three-datapoint minimum). Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because the target's revenue was not available; while the public sector median trades at 23.9x P/S across the five comparable tickers, this multiple cannot be meaningfully applied without disclosed revenue.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $30M to $40M, with a median point of $35M. This range is constrained by reliance on a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow private peer data at the Seed stage and lack of revenue disclosure, which would otherwise enable public multiple anchoring and materially tighten the range.
